newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan businessmen question French water deal.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan businessmen question French water deal.

text.p: The Moroccan businessmen's group CGEM said on Friday that plans by Casablanca authorities to have a French firm run the city's water and electricity systems would bring increased costs to consumers.
Casablanca is negotiating with Lyonnaise des Eaux for it to take over management of the city's water, electricity and public waste systems for 30 years starting in the first quarter of 1997.
The city council is to vote soon on whether to approve the deal for Casablanca, the country's financial centre.
The Confederation Generale des Entreprises du Maroc (CGEM) said on Friday that consumers would end up paying most of the French company's planned investment of 30 billion dirhams ($3.4 billion).
The statement said that under new management charges for water, electricity and waste disposal would also rise.
